facts.text: Jane and Frank Kotter live at 1350 East 85th Street, Brooklyn.
Jane and Frank Kotter leased a Volkswagen Passat for three years from 2018 to 2021.
Jane and Frank Kotter leased the Passat from Metro Volkwagen/Audi located on 11th Avenue and 52nd Street in New York City.
Jane and Frank Kotter recall seeing at least one advertisement for the Passat portraying it as technologically advanced and good for families.
On May 1, 2022, Frank Kotter purchased a new Passat for $30,500.00.
The May 1, 2022 Passat purchase included a standard three-year / 36,000 mile warranty for repairs and defects.
Jane and Frank Kotter purchased a one-year warranty against transmission failure for $500.00.
VW recommends a vehicle inspection every 10,000 miles.
Jane and Frank Kotter understood that, under most warranties, any work done on the car is required to be done at an authorized dealership.
Jane and Frank Kotter parked the Passat on their tree-lined street as they had with the leased vehicle.
On August 1, 2022, Frank Kotter changed the car’s oil himself.
On September 10, 2022, after heavy rainfall, Frank Kotter saw about four inches of water flooding the interior floor of the Passat in both the front and rear.
After the flooding, the car would not start despite many tries.
Frank Kotter checked the windows and doors and found nothing open or ajar and no crack or space through which the water could have entered.
Jane and Frank Kotter called Metro’s service department and had the car towed to Manhattan.
The service manager Josef Schmidt told the Kotters the tow cost was $125.00 and would be borne by the Kotters.
Josef Schmidt told the Kotters he would call them when he determined the problem and prior to commencing repairs.
Josef Schmidt called one day later and told the Kotters the interior carpets were a total loss.
Josef Schmidt told the Kotters the transmission control module (TCM) located under the carpet below the driver’s seat had to be replaced because it was damaged by water that entered the vehicle.
The total cost of repairs was $3,790.00, including $1,100.00 for the carpets and $2,690.00 for the TCM.
Jane and Frank Kotter tried to convince Josef Schmidt that there was a defect and that they did nothing to damage the car or cause the water ingress.
Jane and Frank Kotter argued that because they were within the warranty, everything should be covered.
Josef Schmidt answered that he had heard of such problems and seen it one time.
Josef Schmidt told the Kotters that Volkswagen customer service denied responsibility and said the Kotters failed to clear the area below the windshield of leaves and other debris.
Jane and Frank Kotter paid the repair bill and returned home to Brooklyn.
After doing research on the Internet, Jane and Frank Kotter saw that other Passats had water entry problems due to a blocked plenum drain.
The defendant is Volkswagen.
The plaintiffs are the Kotters.

events.text: Frank Kotter changed the car’s oil himself.
After heavy rainfall, the Passat interior floor flooded and the car would not start.
The Kotters called Metro’s service department and had the car towed to Manhattan; Josef Schmidt set tow cost at $125.
Josef Schmidt called one day later with repair findings: carpets total loss and TCM replacement needed; total repair cost $3,790.
Frank Kotter purchased a new Passat for $30,500.00 with a standard three-year / 36,000 mile warranty and bought a one-year transmission failure warranty for $500.00.
